title: Dispense 150 g of tea using a digital scale
instruction: Dispense 150 grams of tea into the cup on the digital scale. Turn the faucet handle to either side to open it; turning farther increases the flow. Return the handle to the central closed position to stop the flow. The handle does not spring back. Use the scale display and allow the remaining falling tea to land. Finish within 10 grams of 150 grams, with the faucet closed and no overflow.
context: This task simulates real-world situations that require dispensing a precise amount of water.
setup: A calibrated YAM dual-arm workstation holds a fixed beverage dispenser, wooden stand, digital kitchen scale and clear glass cup. The dispenser has a frosted, fluted plastic body approximately 19.7 cm in diameter and 31.1 cm high, a wooden lid and a brass-colored rotary faucet; it starts with 6564.026 g of pale red tea. Its four-legged wooden stand measures 23 x 23 x 18 cm. The scale measures approximately 14.5 x 18.6 x 1.7 cm and has a black plastic body, a brushed-metal top and a 0.1 g display. The empty cup is tared on the scale directly under the outlet; its internal diameter is 8 cm, internal height is 11 cm, wall thickness is 3 mm and bottom thickness is 7 mm, giving a modeled liquid capacity of 552.920 g. The task assembly origin is at world position (0.460, 0.000, 0.7475) m with yaw -90 degrees. Relative to that origin before rotation, the stand and jar are centered at (0, 0), the scale at (0, -0.186) m and the cup at (0, -0.151) m; the outlet is at (0, -0.151, 0.214) m. The faucet begins at 0 degrees, the cup is empty, the display reads 0.0 g, both arms start in the station READY configuration with open grippers, and there is no layout randomization. The dispenser body, stand, scale and cup are fixed in place.
scoring: Binary score: 1.0 if, within 120 simulated seconds, the cup contains between 140.0 and 160.0 g of tea inclusive, the faucet is closed in its central [-10, +10] degree deadband, all airborne tea has landed, and zero flow with no airborne tea has persisted for at least 0.3 seconds, with no overflow at any time. Otherwise the score is 0.0. Passing through the target mass while tea is still flowing does not count. Score uses unrounded simulated liquid mass; numerical overflow below 1e-9 g is treated as zero. No partial credit.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz, equivalent to 120 simulated seconds; the 32 initial history-warmup steps are included. End early on settled success.
reset_notes: Return both arms to the station READY configuration with open grippers; set the faucet angle and angular velocity to zero; empty and tare the cup; remove all airborne tea; clear accumulated overflow and elapsed time; refill the dispenser to 6564.026 g. Keep the same fixed object poses and camera calibration. Evaluation seed: 0.
fidelity: Robot motion and contact with the passive faucet are simulated in PhysX at 240 Hz. The faucet rotates to either side up to 90 degrees, has a central +/-10 degree closed region and no return spring; flow increases linearly to 30 g/s. Each physics step emits a mass-conserving ballistic water slice; its mass is counted only when it reaches the cup's current liquid surface. Reservoir and cup liquid levels follow their volumes, and closing the faucet preserves liquid already in flight. Liquid uses a density of 1 g/mL and is visualized with cylinders, not a fluid solver. The jar, scale, stand and cup are fixed. The model omits splashing, stream interception by other objects, sloshing, liquid forces on containers, scale impact response and sensor noise. Overflow mass is recorded, but runoff and puddles are not rendered. Flow does not depend on reservoir pressure until empty. Product references guide appearance; the valve mechanism and 0.1 g display resolution are task-specific approximations.
scores: Dream-1 recorded trajectory: 0.0, final cup mass 552.920 g with overflow and the faucet still open. Scripted demonstration: 1.0, final cup mass 149.887 g (display 149.9 g), no overflow, completed in 21.233 s. Both saved trajectories were checked against the scoring rule above.
